skill.name: loop-me
skill.description: Interview users about recurring work and turn their answers into clear workflow specifications.
skill.summary: Create build-ready workflow specs through focused questions.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.value_statement: Recurring work is hard to automate when goals and handoffs stay vague. Loop-me interviews you one question at a time and turns answers into build-ready workflow specs.
actual_capabilities: Runs a guided /grilling session focused on workflow specification.
Asks one question at a time and includes a recommended answer.
Identifies recurring loops worth turning into workflows.
Maintains workflow specs in workflows/*.md as the source of truth.
Uses NOTES.md to capture tools, channels, and user terminology.
Defines triggers, checkpoints, briefs, and done criteria for implementers.
limitations: It does not implement the workflows it specifies.
It needs user answers to resolve unclear workflow details.
It focuses on workspace files named by the skill instructions.
It does not force schedules, AI usage, or checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Plan recurring operations
use_cases.description: Turn repeated business tasks into specifications with triggers, handoffs, and review points.

use_cases.title: Prepare automation briefs
use_cases.description: Clarify enough detail for an implementer agent to build without extra questions.

use_cases.title: Map client workflows
use_cases.description: Interview stakeholders and record their tools, channels, terms, and workflow opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Start a workflow spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a workflow for my weekly planning routine. Ask one question at a time.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you already know the workflow to document.

prompt_templates.title: Find useful loops
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my workspace notes and suggest recurring loops that could become workflow specs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you need help finding automation candidates.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an existing spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the workflow spec in workflows/client-onboarding.md and grill me until an implementer could build it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when a draft exists but still has open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare implementation handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this workflow idea into a complete spec with trigger, steps, checkpoint policy, brief format, and definition of done.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for an advanced handoff to an implementation agent.

output_examples.input: Design a workflow for handling new support emails.
output_examples.output: A workflow spec covering the event trigger, triage steps, escalation rules, checkpoint brief, and completion criteria.

output_examples.input: Find workflow opportunities from my notes.
output: A short list of recurring loops found in the workspace.
A recommended first workflow to specify.
Focused questions needed before writing the spec.

output_examples.output: A clearer onboarding workflow with unresolved terms sharpened and open decisions turned into direct questions.

best_practices: Start with the recurring activity and the outcome before discussing tools.
Answer each question with concrete examples from real work.
Keep NOTES.md current when terminology, channels, or tools change.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to implement the workflow before the spec is complete.
Do not treat every workflow as needing AI, schedules, or checkpoints.
Do not skip unclear terms that an implementer would need to know.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates and refines workflow specifications for recurring work in your workspace.

faq.question: Does it build the automation?
faq.answer: No. It prepares the specification that an implementer or implementation agent can use.

faq.question: Why does it ask one question at a time?
faq.answer: Single questions keep the interview focused and reduce incomplete answers.

faq.question: What files does it use?
faq.answer: It uses workflow specs under workflows/*.md and shared context in NOTES.md.

faq.question: Can it suggest workflows I have not named?
faq.answer: Yes. It can look for recurring loops in your work and propose candidates.

faq.question: Does every workflow need a human checkpoint?
faq.answer: No. Checkpoints are added only when the workflow needs human review or decisions.
